chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Allah did not create any creature more numerous than the angels. Indeed, every evening, seventy thousand angels descend from the sky, circumambulating the House (Kaaba) throughout the night. When dawn breaks, they depart to the grave of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), send him greetings, then come to the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and send him greetings. Then they come to the grave of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and send him greetings, then to the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and send him greetings. Then they ascend to the sky before the sun rises. Then the angels of the day, seventy thousand angels, descend and circumambulate the Sacred House throughout the day. When the sun approaches sunset, they depart to the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and send him greetings. Then they come to the grave of the Commander of the Faithful and send him greetings, then to the grave of Al-Hasan and send him greetings, then to the grave of Al-Husayn and send him greetings. Then they return to the sky before the sun sets.'
ai.seo_question: What is the daily routine of angels visiting the graves of the Prophet and Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the continuous celestial worship of the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing a spiritual link between the Kaaba and the graves of the Prophet and Imams. It underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory status of the Imams, as angels prioritize saluting their graves after circumambulating the House of God, reinforcing the concept of *Ziyarat* as a means of connecting with the divine through the chosen servants of Allah.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 46.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  said,  “The  number  of  any creature of Allah is not more than that of angels. Seventy thousand  angels  come  down  to  earth  every  night  and circumambulate the Holy Kaaba all night. They come to the holy grave of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) before sunrise and salute him, then salute Amirul Momineen (a.s.) at his grave, then  salute  Imam  Hasan  (a.s.)  at  his  grave  and  come  to salute Imam Husain (a.s.) at his grave and go back to the heaven before the sun rises. Then seventy thousand angels come  to  earth  during  the  day.  They  circumambulate  the Holy Kaaba all day and salute the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) at his  grave  before  sunset. Then they  come  to salute  Amirul Momineen (a.s.) at his grave, then salute Imam Hasan (a.s.) at his grave and finally they come to salute Imam Husain (a.s.) at his grave and return to heaven before the sun sets.
